$$

$$

This corresponds to the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

The second equation tells us that ${x}_{2}=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get 

$$
{x}_{1}+2(0)=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=0.
$$

So, we conclude that $x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ is the only solution to this system.

Therefore, $\text{Null}(A)=\{0\}.$

We need to solve the equation $Ax=0.$ First, we find the row echelon form of $A$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 7 & -7 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-7){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is ${x}_{1}$, and we have two free variables, ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}.$ That means we need to find ${x}_{1}$ in terms of ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}.$

From the first equation we get ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}-{x}_{3},$ so the set of all the solutions of $Ax=0$ is

$$
\text{Null}(A)=\{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}-{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R\}.
$$

questions.problem: Consider the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ -2 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}]$ and the vector $b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ k \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Find the value of $k$ such that $b\in \text{Null}(A).$
questions.worked_solution:
If $b\in \text{Null}(A),$ then we must have $Ab=0.$ Substituting the given information, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Ab & =0 \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ -2 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ k \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-2k+2 \\ 4k-4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-2k+2=0 \\ 4k-4=0\end{aligned}
$$

and for each of these equations, we obtain $k=1.$
